latin.505: §. V. Expositam hactenus Paulinam de S. Cœna Mentem Sententiamque veram, Christi Verbis Institutionis æquè atque horum Commentario Antecedaneo, Joh. cap. 6. tradito, exactè congruam, totô æræ Christianæ seculô Primô, i. e. Apostolicô, perdurasse, eoque omnium Apostolorum horumque Discipulorum (quos inter Polycarpus, Johannis Discipulus, numeratur) probatam calculo fuisse, haud absurdè intelligi datur.
latin.506: Ex Act. 2. 42., ubi Judæi, mediante Petri sermone, ad Christianismum noviter conversi, iidemque primi omnium, proskarterountes, i. e. assiduè atque perpetuò incumbentes sistuntur, non tantum didachē tōn Apostolōn, Doctrinæ, etiam de Cœna, Apostolicæ, sed & tē koinōnia ab Apostolo 1. Cor. 10. à vers. 16. ad 20. inclusivè expositæ.
latin.507: I. e. tàm cum Christo ejusque corpore & sanguine, quàm inter se, Communioni spirituali, huicq; junctæ tē klasei tou artou, i. e. fractioni panis, to sōma hyper hymōn klōmenon præfiguranti, & semper præfiguraturæ, 1. Cor. 11. 24.
latin.508: Quorum Christianorum puta primorum hoc pacto Communio seu koinōnia fuit, cum Apostolis fuit, & uti istorum, ita ritè communicantium quorumvis, per omnia secula, cum iisdem, eoque simul koinōnia meta tou patros kai meta tou huiou Iēsou Christou, Communio & cum Patre Cœlesti & cum Filio ejus Theanthrōpō Jesu Christo, semperq; mansura, 1. Joh. 1. 3.; at Spiritualis, quandoquidem Christus, utut venit non tō hydati monon, all' en tō hydati kai tō haimati.
latin.509: Tamen id ipsum præstitit hunc in modum, ut to pneuma fuerit to martyroun hoti to pneuma estin hē alētheia, Joh. 5. v. 6. coll. cum Joh. cap. 6. v. 63. h. e. ut Spiritus testatus fuerit, Spiritum esse Veritatem, Spiritum item vivificare, verbaque Christi de participatione Corporis & Sanguinis sui, esse Spiritum & vitam.
latin.510: Ut hôc ipsô, post deductam ab origine, per totius primi Seculi Christiani decursum, veram de S. Cœna Doctrinam, nunc promptô pede ad succedentia Secula liceat nobis pertendere, primorum Patrum testimoniis eandem adstructuris & confirmaturis. Equidem nos hâc operâ levatos per quorundam Protestantium Doctorum egregiam industriam, Pontificias Novitates, circa S. Cœnam demolientium, Joh. Oecolampadii, Philippi Melanchtonis, Martini Chemnitii, Danielis Chamieri, & novissimè Johannis Cosini nec non Joh. Guil. Bajeri, probè novimus; ne tamen Historica hæc Opella nostra hiulca evadat, haud gravabimur ex his ipsis Autoribus, singulorum seculorum saltem puriorum testes pro veritate, vel binos, vel ad summum tres, advocare, in quorum ore & hæc veritas immota perstet, si in antecessum hoc unicum monuerimus, nominatos Veterum Testimoniorum collectores, etsi diversæ Protestantium Sectæ addictos, eadem tamen propemodum ex quinque præsertim Seculis prioribus, hac proculdubio de causa adduxisse, vel non potuisse non adducere, quòd in iis res ipsa solummodò, i. e. duarum rerum, cœlestis & terrestris, Signati & Signi, in legitimo S. Cœnæ usu, præsentia & participatio, citra vel ullum præsentiæ & participationis rei alterius, Signati scil. modum, vel cum hujus solo, duntaxat spirituali modo, ab utraque Protestantium parte concesso, inculcare deprehenduntur.

pass_a.505: §. V. That the Pauline Mind and true Sentence concerning the Sacred Supper set out thus far — exactly congruent both with Christ’s Institution words and with their Antecedent Commentary handed down in John 6 — endured through the whole First age of the Christian era, i.e. the Apostolic, and was approved by the reckoning of all the Apostles and their Disciples (among whom Polycarp, John’s disciple, is numbered), may not absurdly be understood.
pass_a.506: From Acts 2:42, where Jews newly converted to Christianity by Peter’s sermon, and the first of all, are set forth as proskarterountes, i.e. assiduously and continually attending not only to the didachē of the Apostles — Apostolic Doctrine, even concerning the Supper — but also to the koinōnia set out by the Apostle in 1 Cor. 10 from v. 16 to 20 inclusive.
pass_a.507: That is, to spiritual Communion both with Christ and His body and blood and among themselves, and joined to this the breaking of bread (tē klasei tou artou), prefiguring and always to prefigure the body broken for you (1 Cor. 11:24).
pass_a.508: Of which first Christians, so to speak, there was by this pact Communion or koinōnia with the Apostles, and as of those, so of any rightly communicating through all ages with the same, and therewith at once koinōnia with the heavenly Father and with His Son the God-man Jesus Christ, always to remain (1 John 1:3); yet Spiritual, seeing that Christ, although He came not by water only but by water and blood.
pass_a.509: Yet He performed that very thing in this manner, that the Spirit should be the one bearing witness that the Spirit is the truth (1 John 5:6 coll. with John 6:63) — i.e. that the Spirit should have testified that the Spirit is Truth, that the Spirit also quickens, and that Christ’s words concerning participation of His Body and Blood are Spirit and life.
pass_a.510: So that by this very thing, after the true Doctrine concerning the Sacred Supper has been drawn from the origin through the course of the whole first Christian age, we may now with ready foot stretch on to the succeeding ages, the testimonies of the first Fathers about to build and confirm the same. Indeed we know well that we are lightened in this labor by the excellent industry of certain Protestant Doctors demolishing Pontifical Novelties about the Sacred Supper — John Oecolampadius, Philip Melanchthon, Martin Chemnitz, Daniel Chamier, and most lately John Cosin and Joh. Guil. Baier; yet lest this little Historical work of ours gape open, we shall not grudge to call from these very Authors at least two, or at most three, witnesses for the truth of each of the purer ages, in whose mouth this truth too may stand unmoved — if first we warn this one thing: that the named collectors of the Ancients’ Testimonies, though devoted to diverse Protestant sects, nonetheless brought nearly the same from the five earlier ages especially, doubtless for this cause, or could not but bring them, that in them the thing itself alone is found inculcated — i.e. presence and participation of two things, celestial and terrestrial, Signified and Sign, in the lawful use of the Sacred Supper — apart from any mode of presence and participation of the other thing (the Signified), or with its sole, merely spiritual mode, conceded by both Protestant parties.

505: §.V: the Pauline true Supper sentence — matching Institution and the John 6 antecedent commentary — lasted through the whole Apostolic first age.
All the Apostles and their disciples (Polycarp among them, John’s disciple) may fairly be read as approving it.
506: Acts 2:42: Jews newly converted by Peter’s sermon — the first of all — kept attending assiduously (proskarterountes).
Not only to the Apostles’ teaching (didachē), including on the Supper, but also to the koinōnia Paul sets out in 1 Cor. 10:16–20.
507: That koinōnia is spiritual communion with Christ and His body and blood, and among themselves.
Joined to it is the breaking of bread — always prefiguring the body broken for you (1 Cor. 11:24).
508: So the first Christians’ koinōnia with the Apostles — and of every rightly communicating person through all ages — is at once communion with the heavenly Father and with His Son the God-man Jesus Christ (1 John 1:3), always to remain.
Yet it is Spiritual: Christ came not by water only but by water and blood.
509: He did it so that the Spirit should bear witness that the Spirit is the truth (1 John 5:6 with John 6:63).
The Spirit is Truth; the Spirit quickens; Christ’s words on participating His Body and Blood are Spirit and life.
510: Doctrine now traced from the origin through the whole first Christian age — we may step on to later ages with early Fathers to confirm it.
Protestant collectors (Oecolampadius, Melanchthon, Chemnitz, Chamier, Cosin, Baier) already demolished Pontifical novelties; we still take two or three witnesses per purer age from them.

Both sides cite nearly the same from the first five ages: presence of two things (celestial & terrestrial / Signified & Sign) with only the spiritual mode of the Signified conceded. Stop before §.VI (second century: Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus).
